items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee mentions Louis Armstrong only in the context of the venue (Casa Mañana) where Armstrong previously worked, and in relation to Cozy Cole's career ('along the way, after he went with Louis Armstrong'). There is no evidence of a direct personal or professional interaction between Cliff

ctx.x: There is much that we hadn't gone into about the Charlie Barnet band in the forties and '41 and '42. But one of the incidents -- I gave title to, that I thought might be interesting, which I named the Casa Mañana Affair, or, a disaster for us -- when the (bleep) hit the fan for the Charlie Barnet band, and it was some titles of our idols and heroes and how they turn on us, and it goes like this --

We were working at the Casa Mañana Ballroom, or club, it used to be the original Cotton Club when Louie Armstrong worked there, in California, outside of Hollywood. And Duke Ellington's band was playing in the show, Jump for Joy, at a theatre in LA, and Barnet and he got together and talked, as they were so dear friends, and the band and the musicians, that possibly it'd be nice when they finished the theatre on closing night that they had an old fashioned battle of music. It was planned.

And we worked at the Casa Mañana, -- so Barnet, we were all very nervous about the whole thing, because they were our idols, the Ellington band, Duke -- so Barnet came up with a very bright idea. He said pick your own man and find out what his favorite bottle is, what kind of favorite booze he drinks, and let it go from there. We were supposed to supply them with booze and get them stoned, I guess.
